claims.value: Straylight is a user-owned, portable, agent-first context and durable-work layer that preserves learned knowledge together with resumable work state—evidence, decisions, plans, artifacts, computations, checkpoints, and next actions—so later agents can inspect, revise, and advance complex work. It is not primarily a notes or retrieval product.

The token result rejects only the efficiency/justification of the deterministic workspace prototype: it tied one-shot BM25 at 17/20 cases, recovered fewer evidence items (46/53 versus 48/53), and used about 2,932 mean estimated tokens versus 1,070. It does not reject Straylight’s durable-work thesis. The completed follow-on evaluation and owner decision now authorize implementation, with BM25 retained as a regression fixture and cached replay reported separately from uncached input.

The first persistent build slice is a snapshot-pinned typed workspace API that can reopen a revision-N parent checkpoint, refresh it to N+1 with an inspectable constraint/evidence diff, batch query and source reads, combine exact and lexical retrieval with a pluggable semantic path, and atomically commit an immutable child checkpoint containing its parent identifier and preserved source references without reconstructing the unchanged corpus.

The implementation passes its transition gate when every harness case completes in at most four workspace calls, reproduces the claims obtained through direct-filesystem access, exposes the N-to-N+1 diff, and emits an immutable child checkpoint linked to its parent with source lineage intact. Reports must separate cumulative cached replay from uncached input.
